extracted.intended_audience: CIA leadership, OMB officials, and Department/Agency procurement/security heads
extracted.subtask_description: Internal CIA memorandum about OMB Circular A-76 requesting clarification of contracting guidelines for communications, data automation, and other services that touch sensitive intelligence; intended to influence OMB instruction to agency heads to protect security. Focuses on when agencies should avoid contracting functions that would grant contractor access to sensitive intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify contracting guidelines for security-related services
rubrics_metrics.description: That you sign the attached letter to the Director, Office of Management and Budget requesting he clarify contracting guidelines for communication, data automation and other security services relating to sensitive intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action requested is to send an explicit request to OMB to provide clarification. The memorandum frames this as necessary to complete action on the generic issue raised by DOE's attempt to contract out communications services for its all-source center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid contracting services that could diminish security
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask Mr. Stockman to instruct Department and Agency Heads not to contract for services which could diminish security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DCI letter describes concerns that contracting certain services may reduce security protections. The guidance implies agencies should refrain from awarding contracts for functions where contractor performance would adversely affect protection of sensitive intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent unnecessarily broad contractor access to sensitive intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes DCI concerns about unnecessarily broad contractor access to sensitive intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites a concrete example (Department of Energy's attempt to contract communications services for its all-source center) to illustrate the risk that contracting can grant contractors access to sensitive information; implies a standard to limit contractor access and scope of outsourced functions to preserve security.
